# PiG fork of golang.org/x/text v0.43.0 (collate, root locale)

This package is the algorithm of `golang.org/x/text/collate` and `golang.org/x/text/internal/colltab` v0.43.0 (CLDR 23, Unicode 6.2; BSD-3-Clause, `LICENSE`) for one configuration: the root locale (`collate.New(language.Und)`) with the default options. It is a package of the root module (`github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/third_party/collate`). `internal/jsstring/localecompare` uses it for `a.localeCompare(b)`, and `internal/codingagent/tools` for the collation keys of `ls`. For every string it gives the weights, the order and the keys that `collate.New(language.Und)` gives.

x/text keeps the tables of every locale in one set of arrays, 1.25 MB of `uint32` and `uint16`, and links all of them into every binary that uses a collator. The root collator reads about a tenth of them. The fork keeps only what the root collator can read.

## Differences from v0.43.0

1. `collate.go`, `elem.go`, `table.go` and `contract.go` are the code of `collate/collate.go`, `collate/option.go`, `internal/colltab/{collelem,table,contract,iter}.go` for the root locale and the default options: tertiary strength, non-ignorable variable elements, no numeric order, identity level ignored. Options, locale matching (`internal/colltab.MatchLang`), the `[]byte` entry points, the numeric weighter and the unused weight functions are not copied, so `golang.org/x/text/language` is not linked by the collator. The decomposition and Hangul paths call the string lookup on the decomposed bytes in place of a second, byte-slice copy of the same code. `Collator.AppendKey` replaces `KeyFromString`: it appends the key to a slice in place of a `Buffer`.
2. `tables.go` is generated by `go generate` (`gen.go`, which calls `tablegen`) from the `tables.go` of the x/text version that `go.mod` requires. `tablegen` reads the arrays of x/text, walks the trie from the root block of lead bytes exactly as the lookup does, for every byte from 0xC0 to 0xF7 and every continuation byte, and keeps what it reaches: the 128 ASCII elements, the windows of the trie, the expansions that these elements name, and the contraction tries and elements they start. It renumbers them densely and rewrites the indexes inside the elements. Each 64-entry window is stored apart (x/text indexes a window by the continuation byte, 0x80 to 0xBF, so its windows overlap blocks of 64); equal windows are stored once.
3. `collate_xtext_test.go` holds the proof that the fork is x/text for every input (see below). `TestTablesMatchXText` fails when `tables.go` is not what `tablegen` derives from the required x/text version.

## What the tests prove

`go test ./third_party/collate` compares the fork with `golang.org/x/text/collate` (a test-only import):

- the collation key of every code point from U+0000 to U+10FFFF, lone surrogates in WTF-8 included, alone and, for the code points below U+30000, before one or two combining marks;
- the key of every 1-byte, 2-byte and 3-byte byte sequence with a lead byte of 0x80 or above (truncated, overlong and invalid UTF-8 as well), and of every 4-byte sequence with a lead byte from 0xF0 to 0xF7 and continuation bytes;
- every string that the contraction tries match, with a combining mark between the code points of the contraction where Unicode allows it;
- 400,000 pairs from a fixed-seed generator of random strings (combining runs longer than the 30 the iterator reorders, strings longer than its 512-element buffer, Hangul, Han, emoji sequences, noncharacters, lone surrogates and invalid bytes), whose keys and comparison results are equal.

The key of a string lists every primary, secondary and tertiary weight that the comparison reads, so equal keys for these strings mean equal weights.

## Updating

Change `golang.org/x/text` in `go.mod`, run `go generate ./third_party/collate`, then compare the code of `collate` and `internal/colltab` of the new release with these files and repeat their changes. Run `go test ./third_party/collate ./internal/jsstring/...`. Offer nothing upstream without the owner.
